claims.text: US Central Command announced that US forces began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets in Iran at 12:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
US Central Command stated that strikes on IRGC targets were launched in response to attempted attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against US service members.
Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island on the northern side of the Strait of Hormuz during the US attacks.
Iranian news agency Nour News reported explosions in the port cities of Bandar Abbas and Chabahar.
A June Memorandum of Understanding declared an end to fighting that killed thousands in Iran and Lebanon since US and Israeli strikes began on February 28.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated in Bishkek that Iran would immediately reciprocate if the US returns to its commitments under the June memorandum of understanding.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf warned that if the enemy attempts to prevent Iran from exporting oil from the Persian Gulf, no one will be able to export oil.
The Iranian Red Crescent reported four people, including a four-year-old child, were killed and more than 50 injured when missile shrapnel hit a wedding celebration in Sirik, Iran.
US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins stated that the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC.
The IRGC launched a barrage of ballistic missiles at a US Marine base in Aqaba, Jordan, in response to the attack in Sirik.
The Jordanian Armed Forces reported no deaths or injuries resulted from the Iranian missile strike near Aqaba.
US President Donald Trump stated on social media that Iran would be hit again at a much harder and higher level if it retaliates against the US strikes.
Approximately 20% of the world's oil passes through the strategic waterway of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian state media reported US strikes hit a fishmeal factory on Qeshm Island, a fishing pier and maritime tower in Sirik, and an area outside Jiroft Airport.
Japan's 10-year bond yield reached 3% for the first time since 1996 following the market reaction to US strikes in Iran.
US national government debt has risen above $40 trillion.
The US Embassy in Qatar urged Americans in the Middle East to exercise heightened vigilance regarding potential flight cancellations and travel disruptions.
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt announced that Russia was responsible for an August 4 drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport.
An explosive drone discovered near Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport on August 4 failed to detonate due to a faulty detonator.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced the ordered closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn.
Germany announced it will terminate the contract for the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin.
Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova stated Moscow would respond in a mirror-image fashion to Germany's diplomatic measures.
German investigators reported finding double-digit numbers of explosive devices near a power substation in Brandenburg in an attempt to cause a regional power outage.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha warned that Russia's hybrid attack at Leipzig airport is part of a deliberate strategy toward Germany and Europe.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte declared full solidarity with Germany following the Russian hybrid attack in Leipzig.
The drone discovered attached to a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig airport on August 4 was carrying 600 grams of explosives.
Germany is backing the European Commission's 22nd sanctions package covering 1,600 companies and organizations linked to Russia.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Ukrainian drones will continue operating over Russian airspace.
Six Ukrainian railway workers were killed when a Russian ballistic missile hit a locomotive depot in Kyiv on Tuesday.
Since Russia's full-scale invasion began, 58 Ukrainian railway staff have been killed and at least 318 injured.
So far in 2026, Russia has struck Ukraine's railway network more than 1,500 times, damaging 249 carriages and 492 locomotives.
Ukrzaliznytsia operates 15,000 miles of track and employs 170,000 workers, making it Ukraine's largest company.
Overnight Russian strikes on Kyiv killed at least 12 people and injured over a dozen.
Four people were killed in Boryspil, near Kyiv, when a Russian strike hit a residential building.
A 26-year-old Indian national was killed in Boryspil on his birthday during Russian strikes.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged Russian President Vladimir Putin in Kyrgyzstan to move from endless war toward peace.
A Ukrainian drone strike hit the Russian Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga, triggering a fire.
Ukrainian air defences shot down 5 Iskander ballistic missiles, 2 Banderol cruise missiles, 5 Kalibr cruise missiles, and 187 out of 218 drones launched by Russia.
US defence manufacturer Lockheed Martin produces approximately 600 Pac-3 Patriot interceptor missiles per year.
According to AFP analysis, Russian forces captured 35 square miles of Ukrainian territory during August 2026.
